headline: S&P 500 claws back a steep early slide to end down 0.3% as Nvidia sinks 3.9% on credit watch
subhead: Hot October PCE inflation (core 3.3%) cemented bets on a December Fed hike; the Nasdaq fell 0.6%, the 10-year yield eased to 4.85% and WTI rose 2.4% to $84.03 on a Houthi refinery attack claim.

us.text: The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,182.8 and the Nasdaq 0.6% after recovering most of a morning rout; the Dow rose 0.3%.
October PCE rose 3.8% from a year earlier and core PCE 3.3%, leaving a December Fed hike near fully priced alongside new tariff threats.
Nvidia fell 3.9% after S&P put its AA rating on CreditWatch negative; Oracle lost 5.1% as its credit default swaps hit a record.

india.text: After the 24 Nov holiday, the Nifty rose to 25,819.3 on 25 Nov on FII buying and lower crude; the dashboard feed still shows 23 Nov prices.
FIIs bought a net Rs 4,479 crore and DIIs Rs 4,019 crore in the cash market on 25 Nov, per provisional NSE data.
The rupee jumped 69 paise to 92.16 per dollar on 25 Nov, an eight-month high, on equity gains, foreign inflows and softer crude.

global.text: Seoul's Kospi closed below 5,000 on 25 Nov as Samsung and SK hynix slumped, and the Nikkei fell to 57,011.6 on AI chip losses.
European shares closed lower on 24 Nov as the tech rally faded and miners slid; the DAX fell 1.3% and the FTSE 100 0.1%.
Brent settled at $94.61 a barrel after the Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, ahead of the 29 Nov OPEC+ meeting.

weekly.narrative: An AI unwind dominated the week: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut failed to steady sentiment, Nvidia fell 22.9 percent and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6 percent and closed in correction. Near-certain bets on a December Fed hike pushed gold down 8.1 percent and silver 14.4 percent to near 52-week lows, and bitcoin fell 5.8 percent toward its 2026 low. India stood apart as heavy foreign buying lifted the Nifty to a nine-month high of 25,800.6 and Bank Nifty to records, while Tokyo, Seoul and Frankfurt followed Wall Street lower. Next week is shortened by Thanksgiving and turns on US PCE inflation and GDP on 25 November, ahead of the Fed decision on 9 December.
